//: Story Phase 4 crew dialogue, one script per crew member per story state (see data/npcs/phase4_crew.json for the selectors). Generated from a single source so the selectors and scripts stay in step.
hale.p4_s9_1: hale[resigned]: Seven hundred percent. I've had worse forecasts from the Admiralty, Captain. Not many.
hale.p4_s9_2: hale: The watch is set. The bell's coughing. The Center's in the treasure room. As normal days go, it's a normal day.
hale.p4_s8: hale[resigned]: An hour's work. Four seconds. I'm writing it in the log, and then I'm going to sit down.
hale.p4_s7: hale[happy]: Good work on the rail, Captain. That's proper carpentry. Well. It's carpentry.
hale.p4_s6: hale[alarmed]: Captain, I've been at sea thirty years. I've never seen the water do THAT.
hale.p4_s5: hale[annoyed]: The roster's full up for Shark Duty till next Tuesday, Captain. Everyone's volunteered. At knifepoint, but still.
hale.p4_s4: hale[concerned]: The powder, the medicine, the bread. It's like it reads the duty roster, Captain.
hale[resigned]: I've started telling the crew we're doing one thing and then doing another. It doesn't help. But it feels like fighting back.
hale.p4_s3b: hale[resigned]: Three hours' sleep between the lot of us, Captain. I've seen the men nod off on their feet. Finch did it halfway up the ratlines.
hale.p4_s3_1: hale: Where's the Center, Captain? ...Right. Then I'll do the log in the bow. I'm not doing paperwork in a cloud again.
hale.p4_s3_2: hale[resigned]: We've had to split the watches round the bell now. Nobody wants to be the one who rings three.
hale.p4_s2: hale[concerned]: 'Might be now.' He wrote a forecast that said 'might be now', Captain, and then it WAS now.
hale[resigned]: Mind you, it's the first forecast I've ever seen come true that fast.
hale.p4_s1: hale[resigned]: Morning, Captain. Ration's in the galley. I'd hold your breath going down the ladder. Actually, I'd hold it all day.
quill.p4_s9: quill: I've started a separate ledger for the forecasts, Captain. Predicted, actual, and a column for 'why'. The 'why' column is all question marks.
quill.p4_s8: quill[devastated]: I've crossed out the assets.
quill.p4_s7: quill[happy]: One board, one brace, one patch. I've entered them in the ledger as ASSETS, Captain.
quill.p4_s6: quill[alarmed]: I'm writing everything down, Captain. For the inquiry. There will be an inquiry. Won't there?
quill.p4_s5: quill[annoyed]: Shark Duty's the only job on the ship with a hundred percent attendance and a zero percent success rate.
quill.p4_s4: quill[concerned]: I've a list of every room the Center has sat in this week, Captain, and a list of every room we needed. They're the same list.
quill.p4_s3b: quill[sad]: I've been sleeping on the ledger. It's flat. The ledger's the only flat thing on deck that isn't already a bed for somebody.
quill.p4_s3: quill: The bell protocol's mine, Captain. I wanted it short. Four lines. The crew needed something they could remember while running.
quill.p4_s2: quill[annoyed]: Forty percent galley, sixty percent cannon deck. That adds to a hundred before the 'later'. Mathematically it's a disgrace, Captain.
quill[sad]: Well. Mathematically. I've no complaint about the accuracy. It was very accurate. Just early.
quill.p4_s1: quill[concerned]: I've started a ledger for it, Captain. Where the Center was each hour. It's mostly the word 'everywhere'.
mags.p4_s9: mags: Seven hundred percent. I'll double the ration, then. No, don't thank me. Nobody ever thanks me for the ration.
mags.p4_s8: mags[annoyed]: I'm not making the pudding.
mags.p4_s7: mags[happy]: Look at that. Look at them all working. I'll make a pudding. It'll be biscuit, but I'll call it a pudding.
mags.p4_s6: mags[alarmed]: Is she going to hold, Captain? I need to know whether to make supper.
mags.p4_s5: mags: I've got the fresh ration going round the rail, Captain. The sharks like it better than the crew do. I'm taking that personally.
mags.p4_s4: mags[angry]: Bread. It went for the BREAD, Captain. Somebody tell that cloud there's a queue.
mags.p4_s3b: mags[annoyed]: I've been sleeping in the galley, on the flour sacks. It's the only room it hasn't bothered with this week. Now I've said that, it will.
mags.p4_s3: mags: Where's it sitting today? If it's the galley, it's biscuit. If it's not the galley, it's still biscuit, because it'll BE the galley by noon.
mags.p4_s2: mags[angry]: My galley's full of it again, Captain. Breakfast, the bread, the table, my good ladle.
mags[annoyed]: I'll get it back. I always get it back. It'll just smell like a Tuesday.
mags.p4_s1: mags[annoyed]: One ration each. Don't ask for seconds. There are seconds. You don't want them.
fennimore.p4_s9: fennimore: Seven hundred percent. Medically speaking, Captain, I'd say that's about right. Take deep breaths. Not here.
fennimore.p4_s7: fennimore[happy]: No injuries on the repair. That's a first. I've written it down twice so I remember what it felt like.
fennimore.p4_s6: fennimore[alarmed]: If she goes down, Captain, I'd like it noted that I was against this voyage from the beginning. I wasn't, but I'd like it noted.
fennimore.p4_s5: fennimore[concerned]: Four bites, Captain. All on poles, thank heavens. I've been bandaging the poles.
fennimore.p4_s4: fennimore[annoyed]: Wick still has that splinter. It's become a sort of pet. He's named it.
fennimore.p4_s3b: fennimore[concerned]: Nobody's sleeping. I'd prescribe rest, but I'd have to prescribe somewhere to have it.
fennimore.p4_s3: fennimore: I've written 'WHERE IS THE CENTER' on the back of every splint, Captain. The crew check before they break anything now. That's progress.
fennimore.p4_s2: fennimore[annoyed]: I've had six men this morning asking me if 'might be now' counts as a diagnosis.
fennimore.p4_s1: fennimore[concerned]: Three breaths of the Center and a grown man's on the floor, Captain. Five if he's Brask. I've been keeping notes.
brask.p4_s9: brask[annoyed]: Seven hundred percent. I've had my worst fears confirmed before, Captain. Never in crayon.
brask.p4_s8: brask[annoyed]: Right. That's it. I'm loading grape. Nobody stop me. ...Somebody stop me.
brask.p4_s7: brask[happy]: Good rail, that. You could lean a cannon on that. Please don't.
brask.p4_s6: brask[alarmed]: Captain, there's a hammerhead out there using our hull as a door knocker.
brask.p4_s5_1: brask[annoyed]: One shot, Captain. One shot of grape into the water. I'd clear the lot.
brask.p4_s5_2: brask[annoyed]: No? The noise? Fine. FINE. I'll poke them. Like an animal.
brask.p4_s4: brask[annoyed]: Gunnery drill's cancelled again. The powder's in it. Every. Single. Drill.
brask.p4_s3b: brask[annoyed]: I've slept on a gun carriage before, Captain. In a battle. That was more restful than this.
brask.p4_s3: brask: Where's the Center? Good. Then I'm cleaning Old Bess in the waist, where I can see it coming.
brask.p4_s2: brask[annoyed]: Sixty percent on the cannon deck by noon. I've moved the powder anyway. Just in case the fool's right for once.
brask.p4_s1: brask[disgusted]: Grog with a skin on it. I've had grog with a lot of things in it, Captain. Never a skin.
nell.p4_s9: nell: Course is set, Captain. Behind us, all the way to the horizon, there's a yellow line on the sea. I'm trying not to think of it as a signpost.
nell.p4_s8: nell[concerned]: She's not grateful any more.
nell.p4_s7: nell[happy]: She sits better already. You can feel it at the wheel. She's grateful.
nell.p4_s6: nell[alarmed]: She's listing to port, Captain. Only a little. Only a little is how it starts.
nell.p4_s5: nell[concerned]: The sharks are following our wake, Captain. I could lose them with a change of course, if they didn't follow the smell instead of the ship.
nell.p4_s4: nell[annoyed]: I've tied a yellow ribbon to the wheel. If it's damp in the morning, the Center's been sitting on it. It's always damp.
nell.p4_s3b: nell[concerned]: Nobody on the wheel after midnight if it's anywhere near the quarterdeck. We just let her drift and hope. I hate hoping, Captain. It's not navigation.
nell.p4_s3: nell: I check where the Center is before I take the wheel now. Then I check again. Then I take the wheel, and hold my breath, and check again.
nell.p4_s2: nell[annoyed]: The forecast had an arrow pointing straight at the helm, Captain. And one pointing away. And one that went round in a circle. I've chosen to ignore all three.
nell.p4_s1: nell: Steady south-sou'west, Captain. Assuming nothing sits on the wheel today. Which it won't. Probably.
wick.p4_s9: wick[concerned]: Seven hundred, Captain. Is that a lot? Mister Quill says it's a lot. I think it's a lot.
wick.p4_s8: wick[sad]: Somebody's going to have to tell Jory about the nails. I'm not doing it.
wick.p4_s7: wick[happy]: I held the nails, Captain! Jory said I held them very well!
wick.p4_s6: wick[alarmed]: Captain? The ship's making a noise like my granny's knees.
wick.p4_s5: wick[concerned]: I asked for Shark Duty, Captain. I didn't ask for it. Mister Hale said I asked for it.
wick.p4_s4: wick[sad]: I've still got the splinter. I call it Cedric. Doc says that's not healthy. Doc says a lot of things.
wick.p4_s3b: wick[sad]: I sleep with my head in a bucket now, Captain. For the air. It isn't much air. But it's MY air.
wick.p4_s3: wick: Where's the Center, Captain? I have to take the slops forward and I'm not doing it if it's in the bow again.
wick.p4_s2: wick[sad]: I left my breakfast in there. And my cap. And I think a bit of my courage.
wick.p4_s1: wick[concerned]: Morning, Captain. Is it true the Center can find you if you think about it too much? I've been trying not to think about it. It's hard.
rook.p4_s9: rook: Seven hundred. Yeah. I'd have said eight, personally, but you've got to trust the professionals.
rook.p4_s8: rook[annoyed]: I'm not marrying anything ever again.
rook.p4_s7: rook[happy]: That's a lovely brace. I'd marry that brace.
rook.p4_s6: rook[alarmed]: They're EATING her, Captain! Actually EATING her!
rook.p4_s5: rook[annoyed]: I've done three shifts. My arms are all pole now. I have to hold my spoon like a pole.
rook.p4_s4: rook[annoyed]: I don't even ask where it is any more, Captain. I just ask where we need to go, and go the other way.
rook.p4_s3b: rook[annoyed]: Sleep? I lay down on the deck and a gull stood on me. That was the most rest I had.
rook.p4_s3: rook: Where's it today? ...Right. Then I'm scrubbing this bit of deck, and if it comes, I'm scrubbing that bit.
rook.p4_s2: rook[annoyed]: 'Bad here. Probably.' I could have told him that. I could have told him that for FREE.
rook.p4_s1: rook[disgusted]: Is it just me, or is the grog looking at us?
sully.p4_s9: sully: Tomorrow's seven hundred percent, is it? I'll wear two masks.
sully.p4_s7: sully[happy]: Good job, that. Tight. Tidy. I'd put my name on it, but it's a rope.
sully.p4_s6: sully[alarmed]: The patch is gone. The patch for the patch is gone. The BUCKET is gone!
sully.p4_s5: sully[annoyed]: The mop's the worst tool. The shark doesn't mind the mop. The shark thinks the mop is a present.
sully.p4_s4: sully[sad]: I needed the privy this morning. It was in the privy. I'm not saying anything else about it.
sully.p4_s3b: sully[sad]: My hammock's still down there. It's in the Center. It's probably having a better night than me.
sully.p4_s3: sully: Where's the Center? I've got to fetch rope from the hold and I'm not going down there on a guess.
sully.p4_s2: sully[annoyed]: My mug was in there. My GOOD mug. The one with a handle.
sully.p4_s1: sully[disgusted]: I'm not drinking it. I'm going to hold it and look like I'm drinking it. Nobody check.
finch.p4_s9: finch: Seven hundred percent. When I was a boy, the forecast was 'wind'. I miss wind.
finch.p4_s8: finch[sad]: Nobody's writing songs about that.
finch.p4_s7: finch[happy]: Now THAT's seamanship. Hammer, nail, done. Nobody writes songs about it, but they should.
finch.p4_s6: finch[alarmed]: I've seen a ship go down, Captain. It started with a noise like that.
finch.p4_s5: finch: In my day, Captain, a shark was a shark. You saw one and you said 'there's a shark'. Now I say 'there's a shark' about every four seconds.
finch.p4_s4: finch[concerned]: It's cleverer than it looks, that cloud. And it looks like a cloud, so that's not saying much, but still.
finch.p4_s3b: finch[sad]: I sleep standing up now, like a horse. It's not a skill I wanted to learn at my age.
finch.p4_s3: finch: Where's the Center today, Captain? My knees used to tell me the weather. Now they just tell me when to run.
finch.p4_s2: finch: The old sailors used to say never trust a forecast from a man in a sash. I've just made that up. But they'd have said it.
finch.p4_s1: finch[concerned]: Forty years at sea, Captain, and I never once asked where the air was before breakfast.
jory.p4_s9: jory: Every plank on the port side's been patched, Captain. Most of them twice. I've run out of chalk writing PATCH FOR PATCH.
jory.p4_s7: jory[happy]: Look at her, Captain. Rail, brace, patch. That's a day's work in an hour. That's the best work I've done all week.
jory.p4_s6: jory[alarmed]: My patch! My PATCH! That patch was PERFECT!
jory.p4_s5: jory[determined]: Keep them off the patch, Captain. Anywhere else, fine. Not the patch.
jory.p4_s4: jory[determined]: I've started chalking the date on every repair. It's how you know when you did it. It's also how you know how long it lasted.
jory.p4_s3b: jory[annoyed]: The hammocks are reactivating again, Captain. I won't explain what that means. I don't want to say it out loud.
jory.p4_s3: jory: Where's the Center? I've a hinge to fix on the washroom door and I'm not doing it again with Gristle stuck on the other side.
jory.p4_s2: jory[annoyed]: I'll have to go in and fix that galley bench after it's been sat on by the Center all morning. The wood goes soft. It goes soft and WARM.
jory.p4_s1: jory: Morning, Captain. The patch is holding. The patch for the patch is holding. Everything's holding, for now.
bob.p4_s9: bob: Seven hundred percent chance of stink. You know what, Captain? I'll take it. At least he's stopped pretending it'll be nice.
bob.p4_s7: bob[happy]: That's a good patch. I watched every nail go in. It made me feel better about life.
bob.p4_s6: bob[alarmed]: Captain, is the ship going to be all right? Just say yes. You don't have to mean it.
bob.p4_s5: bob[sad]: I'm on Shark Duty after this. I've been practising. On the mast. The mast doesn't bite back, but I'm getting my aim in.
bob.p4_s4: bob[concerned]: I asked Garrick where it'd be tomorrow. He drew me a picture of a goose. I don't know what that means. I don't think he does.
bob.p4_s3b: bob[sad]: Nobody's slept properly in a week. I've started sleeping in the rigging. It's windy, but at least the wind is ordinary.
bob.p4_s3: bob: Where's the Center, Captain? I've got to go down for my other shirt, and I'm not going down if it's wearing it.
bob.p4_s2: bob[sad]: My breakfast's still in there. The good biscuit. I can see it from the hatch. It's just sitting there, being yellow.
bob.p4_s1: bob[sad]: I miss rum, Captain. Proper rum. You'd pour it and it would just be rum. It wouldn't do anything.
ned.p4_s9: ned[concerned]: They're all along the wake now, Captain. All the way back. Like a road.
ned.p4_s8: ned[concerned]: Three hundred more. I'm not counting the ones behind them.
ned.p4_s7: ned: Fewer on the port side since the Center moved off. Only a couple of hundred. That's a relief. Hear me: a couple of hundred is a RELIEF.
ned.p4_s6: ned[alarmed]: I can't count them any more, Captain. There's no gaps between them to count.
ned.p4_s5: ned[concerned]: Counting, Captain. Always counting. I've run out of fingers. I'm using Wick's.
ned.p4_s4: ned[concerned]: I'm counting more of them every morning. It's not going down. It's never going down.
ned.p4_s3b: ned[concerned]: More fins at night, Captain. They seem to like the dark. Or the smell's stronger when it's cold.
ned.p4_s3: ned: I call out where the Center is now, as well as sails. It's got its own shout. 'CENTER, BY THE MAINMAST, MOVING SLOW.' I'm quite proud of it.
ned.p4_s2: ned[concerned]: I watched the Center go into the galley from up here, Captain. It went in the hatch like a cat going under a door.
ned.p4_s1: ned: Quiet water this morning, Captain. A few fins, keeping their distance. They'll close in when they've had breakfast.
jim.p4_s9: jim: Seven hundred percent. I'll put the stew on early. Get it done before it notices.
jim.p4_s8: jim[sad]: I'm not doing the stew.
jim.p4_s7: jim[happy]: Proper repair, that. I'll do a stew tonight. A new stew. A HOPEFUL stew.
jim.p4_s6: jim[alarmed]: If she sinks, Captain, I want it on record that there was still biscuit in the hold.
jim.p4_s5: jim[annoyed]: I've been giving the sharks the burnt bits. Mags says I'm encouraging them. They were already encouraged.
jim.p4_s4: jim[angry]: The OVEN. It sat on the OVEN. There was BREAD in the oven. It knew. It KNEW.
jim.p4_s3b: jim[sad]: I dream about that stew, Captain. It was going to be a good stew.
jim.p4_s3: jim: Where is it? Don't tell me it's the galley. Don't. ...Is it the galley?
jim.p4_s2: jim[angry]: My pancakes are IN THE CENTER. A week of flour, Captain. A WEEK of flour.
jim.p4_s1: jim[annoyed]: Pancakes. I made pancakes. Nobody's asked for a pancake. Everyone's looking at the grog.
gristle.p4_s9: gristle: Seven hundred. Fine. I've already got my toothbrush. I'm ready for anything.
gristle.p4_s8: gristle[annoyed]: I want it known I'm thinking very positively about Garrick right now. Positively overboard.
gristle.p4_s7: gristle[happy]: I've got to say, Captain, it's nice to fix something. It's nice to fix something that isn't a crewmate.
gristle.p4_s6: gristle[alarmed]: I've seen a lot of bad days on this ship, Captain. This one's got a special sort of look.
gristle.p4_s5: gristle[annoyed]: I'm taking a double shift. I've got a lot of feelings to work out, and the sharks have noses.
gristle.p4_s4: gristle: The rigging's the only safe place on this ship, Captain. It's never been in the rigging. Yet. Don't tell it I said that.
gristle.p4_s3b: gristle[annoyed]: I won't go in the washroom now without someone at the scuttle. Pete does it. Pete's very good. He doesn't shout advice.
gristle.p4_s3: gristle[annoyed]: Twelve minutes in there, Captain. Twelve. I held my breath for the first three and then I just... had to think positive.
gristle.p4_s2: gristle[annoyed]: 'Forecasts change.' I'll change HIS forecast.
gristle.p4_s1: gristle[disgusted]: It's got LUMPS, Captain. Grog shouldn't have lumps. Porridge has lumps. Grog has... grog.
penhallow.p4_s9: penhallow[annoyed]: Seven hundred percent. I'm writing it down for my memoirs. Nobody will believe me.
penhallow.p4_s8: penhallow[offended]: That's not a thing that happens on tea clippers.
penhallow.p4_s7: penhallow[smug]: Adequate work. I've seen better on a Portuguese tea clipper. Much better. Very clean.
penhallow.p4_s6: penhallow[terrified]: If this ship sinks with me aboard, my company will be FURIOUS.
penhallow.p4_s5: penhallow[terrified]: They wanted ME to take a pole. I'm a PRISONER. I've never been so insulted, and I've been kidnapped.
penhallow.p4_s4: penhallow: When I'm ransomed, Captain, I'm going to tell everyone it was the smell that broke me. Not the chains. The smell.
penhallow.p4_s3b: penhallow[offended]: They moved me to the deck with everyone else. Captivity used to be private, Captain.
penhallow.p4_s3: penhallow[annoyed]: Where is it today? I'd like to plan my captivity around it.
penhallow.p4_s2: penhallow[offended]: I paid good money for passage on a pirate ship. Well. I was CAPTURED by a pirate ship. The principle stands.
penhallow.p4_s1: penhallow[disgusted]: I was a merchant, Captain. I sold tea. Nobody ever warned me about any of this.
dunstan.p4_s9: dunstan: Seven hundred percent. On the middle watch, that'll be about nine hundred.
dunstan.p4_s8: dunstan: I'll keep an eye on the gap where it was.
dunstan.p4_s7: dunstan: Nice work. I'll keep an eye on it on the middle watch. I'll watch it very hard.
dunstan.p4_s6: dunstan: I'd better go and wake the rest of the watch. They'll want to see this. They won't want to, but they'll want to.
dunstan.p4_s5: dunstan: My shift's midnight to four. The sharks don't sleep. I haven't slept either. We have that in common.
dunstan.p4_s4: dunstan: The Center and me keep the same hours now, Captain. I think it's starting to recognise me.
dunstan.p4_s3b: dunstan: They've put me on the deck with the others. Snoring, coughing, somebody shouting 'NOT THE PILLOW' in their sleep.
dunstan.p4_s3: dunstan: Where's it tonight? I only ask because I'm on the middle watch and it's always on the middle watch.
dunstan.p4_s2: dunstan: I've given up guessing, Captain. I just follow Pete. Pete's got a nose for it. Pete's got a nose for everything now.
dunstan.p4_s1: dunstan: Morning, Captain. Middle watch. I saw the Center go past twice in the night. It didn't stop. It just went. Like it was busy.
hale.p4_sleep_hint: hale[resigned]: Get some sleep, Captain. In your own bed, while it's still yours.
hale: Tomorrow's another day. Probably a worse one. But another one.
hale.p4_protocol_hint: hale: Read the protocol first, Captain. It's nailed to the foremast, by the bell.
jim.p4_damper_hint: jim[angry]: The DAMPER, Captain. On the stovepipe. Forward of the hatch. Before my galley burns down round the Center.
jim.p4_lunch_hint: jim[sad]: Biscuit crate's in the hold, Captain. Down through the galley, down the stairs. Mind the stove. Well. Mind the Center. The stove's past minding.
jory.p4_report_hint: jory: The poles are in the barrel, Captain. Right here beside me. Pick the long one.
jory.p4_repairs_hint: jory[determined]: Board, brace, patch, Captain. All on the port rail. Face the rail and get stuck in.
nell.p4_helm_hint: nell[concerned]: The wheel, Captain! Up the stairs, at the stern. She's still falling off!
